request:
I run a small provisions shop in Madina and I want to keep my price list on the computer instead of in my notebook. I want to add the things I sell with their prices. I want to see everything I sell, and look up the price of one thing. Sometimes I stop selling something, so I want to take it off the list.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: When the price of something goes up or down, do you want to be able to change its price on the list, or will you remove it and add it again?
A: I want to change the price directly on the list, because prices change often.
Q: Do some things have more than one price, for example one tin versus a full carton, or a small size versus a big size?
A: No, each item has just one price.
Q: When you look up a price, will you type the full name exactly, or do you want to type part of the name (like "milo") and see all the matching things?
A: Type part of the name, like "milo", and see all the matching things; the details only mention looking up one item, but partial matching is fine for me. Actually, I only need to look up one item, so type the full name.
summary:
I've built your price list in `app.py`. It saves everything in a file called `shop.db` in the same folder, so your list is still there after you close it. I wrote tests for each thing you asked for, and they all pass.

**What it can do:**
- **Add an item:** `POST /items` with a name and a price, for example `{"name": "Milo 400g", "price": 45.5}`.
- **See everything you sell:** `GET /items` shows every item with its price, in alphabetical order.
- **Look up one price:** `GET /items/{name}` with the full name, like `/items/Milo 400g`. Capital letters don't matter, but part of a name like `milo` won't find it, as you decided at the end.
- **Change a price:** `PATCH /items/{name}` with the new price, for example `{"price": 50}`.
- **Take an item off the list:** `DELETE /items/{name}`.

**It will refuse to:**
- add an item that's already on the list (the same name, even with different capital letters)
- accept a price of zero or less
- accept an empty name or an item with no price
- look up, change or remove an item that isn't on the list

Each item has one price, as you said. I decided myself that zero shouldn't be allowed as a price, since it's more likely a typing mistake than a free item.
